resources.string: Counts how many reels/short videos you scroll so ScrollKiller can show your daily total. It reads only scroll events in short-video feeds and which app is currently in the foreground (so the counter bubble can appear over that app and hide when you leave it) — never the videos, captions, messages, or anything you view. Nothing you look at ever leaves your phone.
One permission to count your scrolling
ScrollKiller uses an Accessibility Service to notice when you swipe through reels and short videos, so it can count them.

It reads only scroll events — the swipe itself. It never reads the videos, captions, messages, passwords, or anything else on your screen. Nothing you view ever leaves your phone; only your daily counts are stored.
Android has no other way for an app to know you\'re doomscrolling in another app. This is the permission that makes the counter — and the blocking — possible.
Find \"ScrollKiller Detector\" in the list, open it, and turn the toggle On. Then press Back to return here.
Show your live count over reels while you scroll
Delete every stored count on this device
This deletes all your scroll counts on this device. It can\'t be undone.
See your count without leaving the app

Let ScrollKiller float a tiny bubble — a brain and your live count — on top of reels while you scroll. You watch the number climb without opening ScrollKiller. It shows only inside tracked short-video apps and disappears everywhere else. This is optional: counting still works without it.
Turn on \"Allow display over other apps\" for ScrollKiller, then press Back to return here.

string-array.item: You\'ve hit your limit. Your brain will thank you.
That\'s enough reels for today. Go touch grass.
The feed will still be there tomorrow. Your time won\'t.
You came here to relax, not to disappear. Take a break.
